subject: Priority pin & emergency traffic triage for Cardinal HealthTech — AZ1 latency + 5xx spike
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha@cardinalhealthtech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <m.michael@cardinalhealthtech.com>, ops@cardinalhealthtech.com
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: Large latency spike & 5xx surge (AZ1) affecting checkout

Monica —

We’re seeing a major degradation in production beginning ~08:45 PDT across our checkout endpoints. TL;DR: p95 latency jumped to ~3.2s (usually ~120ms), 5xx rate at ~8% for the last 20 minutes, and overall throughput to Redwood is down ~30% for our region (AZ1). Users are mid-checkout; conversions are dropping.

We opened our side and verified nothing on our deploy. Can your team confirm whether this looks like a regional routing/serve issue? We need:
- Immediate mitigation (failover or traffic steer)
- Expected impact to sessions/cookies if we do cross-region steer
- ETA for stabilization

This is P0 for us. Please escalate as needed — we’ll keep our product and ops teams on the line.

Attaching a screenshot of real-time metrics and a CSV snapshot of 1-minute KPIs.

— Asha
Asha Menon
Head of Platform Engineering | Cardinal HealthTech
asha@cardinalhealthtech.com

Attachment stubs: cardinal_incident_screenshot.png (PNG), kpi-snapshot.csv (CSV)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha@cardinalhealthtech.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Large latency spike & 5xx surge (AZ1) affecting checkout

Asha — thanks for the flag and the attachments; we see the same on our telemetry. I’m opening an incident and looping in SRE now. Immediate plan (short bullets):

- Triage: SRE to validate whether AZ1 serving hosts are impacted (queue lengths, 5xx surface).
- Mitigate: Requesting temporary Priority Pin to route Cardinal traffic to US-WEST-2 as an emergency steer — this is a routing change that should be quick but requires exec approval for priority allocation if we need to exceed reserved capacity.
- Canary: If approved, we’ll canary at 10% traffic for 3 minutes, check error/latency regressions, then move to 100% if stable.
- Data residency: There may be a brief session-affinity mismatch while KV caches warm — we’ll provide guidance for session fallback.

Can you confirm: are you OK with a cross-region steer to US-WEST-2 for up to 60 minutes while we stabilize? If yes I’ll ask SRE to act and request the priority pin.

I’ve attached the incident stub in our tracker and will keep you updated.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0137

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Asha Menon <asha@cardinalhealthtech.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: Large latency spike & 5xx surge (AZ1) affecting checkout

Monica / Asha —

Quick technical update from SRE after an initial sweep:
- Root symptom: increased queueing on AZ1 GPU frontends, correlated with a model shard hot-spot on several serving nodes. We are also seeing elevated KV cache misses on the most common prefixes.
- Impact: elevated p95 and transient 5xx as workers hit tokenization/throughput backpressure.
- Safe mitigations in order of speed:
  1) Emergency routing (steer) to US-WEST-2 with canary (low risk) — recommended first step.
  2) Manual pod restart of the hot nodes in AZ1 (higher risk of brief 502s during restart).
  3) Rollback to earlier quantized model variant (if routing not possible) — significant quality regression risk.

Notes on steering: KV cache warm-up in the target region will add ~30–90s of elevated latency for affected sessions as we rebuild per-prefix caches; however, overall p95 should drop back toward baseline once warm.

I’m ready to trigger the canary steer if we get authorization for a Priority Pin allocation for Cardinal for the next 60 minutes — that will give us reserved capacity in the target pool and avoid thrashing under load. If execs prefer we can do an unpinned steer but that risks hitting other customers’ shared pools.

Attaching KPI snapshot you sent for internal triage.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Thanks team — ACK and I’m authorizing emergency Priority Pin for Cardinal HealthTech for up to 60 minutes. Please follow the canary plan:

- Step 1: 10% canary to US-WEST-2 for 3 minutes — monitor p50/p95 and 5xx.
- Step 2: If stable, advance to 100% in 5 minutes.
- Step 3: Keep Cardinal CS (Marissa) as the communications lead for customer updates.
- Step 4: We’ll approve a one-time credit waiver for any overage incurred during this emergency; finance will need the postmortem and cost estimate.

Sean — please proceed and post a short timeline in JIRA RED-4521. Monica / Marissa — coordinate the customer update cadence (we should do a 30-min and 2-hr check-in).

Best,

Asha / Michael —

Update: we executed the canary at 10% at ~10:20 PDT, observed p95 drop from ~3.2s to ~220ms and 5xx reduced to <0.5%. We advanced to 100% at ~10:28 PDT and traffic remained stable through the afternoon. AZ1 shows partial recovery; we left Cardinal routed to US-WEST-2 as the controlled mitigation while SRE continues to investigate the AZ1 hot-shard.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- SRE to produce an interim timeline (attached) and postmortem draft in JIRA RED-4521 by EOD tomorrow.
- CS / Monica to run a customer-facing after-action with Cardinal tomorrow at 09:00 PDT — Marissa will lead.
- Finance: Hannah authorized a one-time credit waiver pending postmortem and cost estimate. Monica will coordinate billing artifacts.

Thanks for fast coordination everyone. Asha — please let us know if you need any additional logs or session-level artifacts; we can provide anonymized request traces.

— Monica
